findings.title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered rule list
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, while the other two branches still pass `key={key}`. The previously rendered `GrafanaRuleLoader` had `key={key}`. React will emit "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings and, because this list grows incrementally via infinite scrolling, element reuse becomes index-based, which can cause incorrect DOM/state reuse (e.g. open menus or skeletons attached to the wrong rule) when batches are appended.

findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items are still gated on `rulerRule`, so they disappear in the new list view
findings.body: The menu now computes Grafana-Prometheus-based abilities (`grafanaPauseAbility`, `grafanaDeleteAbility`) so actions can work without ruler data, but the render conditions were not updated: line 123 requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` for the pause item and line 165 requires `rulerRule` for the delete item. The new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons) only passes `promRule`, never `rulerRule`, so Pause/Resume and Delete silently vanish from the rule menu in the alert list for all Grafana-managed rules. The newly added ability checks have no effect for these two actions.

findings.title: Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer can never open without a ruler rule
findings.body: `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` when this component is used from the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule`). Meanwhile AlertRuleMenu now enables the "Silence notifications" item based on the Grafana Prometheus abilities, so the item is visible but clicking it only toggles `showSilenceDrawer` and nothing is rendered — a dead menu entry for every Grafana rule in the list view.

findings.title: skipToken path returns `Duplicate` as supported and allowed, leaking the action onto non-Grafana rules
findings.body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken, ...)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`. With `rule === undefined`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` and `duplicateSupported = true`; `Duplicate` therefore evaluates to `[true, ctx.hasPermission(grafana rules create)]`. Because AlertRuleMenu ORs the ruler and Grafana abilities, a user holding Grafana `AlertingRuleCreate` will see the "Duplicate" action on data-source (Mimir/Loki/Prometheus) rules even when the ruler-based ability says it is unsupported/not allowed, and the clone flow will then fail. The skip path should produce all-false abilities. Note the unit tests mock these hooks, so this is not caught by RulesTable.test.tsx.

findings.title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause and Export support in the new ability hook
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where the ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules). As a result `Pause`, `Restore`, `DeletePermanently` and `ModifyExport` are reported as unsupported for Grafana-managed *recording* rules, even though these rules can be paused and exported. In the list view (which now relies solely on these abilities) pausing/exporting a Grafana recording rule becomes impossible.

findings.title: Federated rule group detection dropped from useAllRulerRuleAbilities
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to mark Update/Delete/Duplicate/Pause as unsupported for federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups. After merging into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `isFederated` is hardcoded to `false` with only a TODO. Users will now be offered Edit/Delete/Duplicate on federated Mimir rules, which cannot be edited through this UI and will fail server-side. If the group information is not available in `RuleGroupIdentifierV2`, this needs another source rather than a silent `false`.

findings.title: `returnTo` query param dropped from the rule view link
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops the `returnTo` parameter, so navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" affordance that the rest of the alerting UI relies on.

findings.title: Test asserts exactly 4 menu items, codifying the loss of Delete/Pause actions
findings.body: The test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` and `AlertingRuleUpdate` both globally and on the folder, yet asserts `menuItems.length === 4` and never uses the newly declared `ui.menuItems.delete` selector. Because the menu still requires a ruler rule for Delete and Pause (AlertRuleMenu lines 123/165), those items are absent — and this assertion now locks that regression in, so a future fix restoring Delete/Pause would break the test instead of the test catching the missing actions. The test should explicitly assert the expected presence of Delete and Pause for a user with those permissions.

findings.title: New `provenance` field on GrafanaPromRuleDTO is untested and unverified against the API
findings.body: `provenance?: string` is added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and is now the only signal used by `isProvisionedPromRule` / `GrafanaRuleListItem`'s `isProvisioned` and by the ability hooks to block editing of provisioned rules in the list view. No test (including the new `rulerRuleToPromRule` helper in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx) sets this field, so if the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not return `provenance`, provisioned rules will be rendered as editable/deletable in the list view and nothing will catch it.

findings.title: `logWarning` called from the render phase
findings.body: `getEditableIdentifier` is invoked during render and calls `logWarning(...)` as a side effect when no identifier can be derived. Render-phase side effects run on every re-render (and twice per render under React StrictMode), so a single rule whose identifier cannot be constructed will repeatedly emit the same analytics warning. This should be moved into an effect or deduplicated.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name after removing the ruler prefetch
findings.body: The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX ... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead readers about what this block does.
